solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cautious about frightening, one having escaped

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: something that has escaped has got out, so this letter leaves the word

parts.note: a hairy moment is a frightening one
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone wary of scary things after one of them has got loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightening' wants to be a synonym of the definition, but hairy is the sense needed, with 'having escaped' removing the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Chary is a synonym of wary or cautious, especially about taking risks.

clue.text: Opportunist appearing in court, shortly

indicators.note: said briefly, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Chancery is a division of the English High Court

explanation.surface: A shifty character turning up in a courtroom for a quick hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts the last letter, Y, from CHANCERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer is British slang for someone who grabs any opportunity, often unscrupulously.

clue.text: Housing agreement

definitions.meaning: a place to live or stay, lodging
a settlement or compromise reached between parties

explanation.surface: A deal about where people will live.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both lodgings provided for people and a compromise reached between two sides.

clue.text: What happens to a baby at a christening? Anything?

definitions.text: What happens to a baby at a christening?
definitions.meaning: the infant is given a name, read playfully as an instruction to the parent
a phrase offering any choice at all

explanation.surface: A question about baptisms followed by an offer of whatever you like.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is cryptic: at a christening the baby is literally given a name, by you.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said after a list to mean whatever else you can think of, anything at all.

clue.text: Played initially, recent or old gramophone record

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the latter of two is the more recent one

explanation.surface: A disc, new or vintage, that has just been spun.
explanation.definitionFit: Platter was old slang, especially in America, for a gramophone disc.

clue.text: Foul place to clear

parts.note: to place something is to put it
to rid a space is to clear it

explanation.surface: A dirty spot that needs clearing out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something putrid is rotten and foul-smelling, a synonym of foul.

clue.text: When pressure generated by snake

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Wondering when a snake builds up pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: The asp is a small venomous snake of Egypt, famous from Cleopatra's death.

clue.text: Deviously test Hals' most important painting

indicators.note: something done deviously is done in a twisted roundabout way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: upper, as in upper classes, means highest in rank

explanation.surface: A sly examination of the Dutch painter Frans Hals's greatest work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deviously' rearranges TEST HALS into THE LAST, before SUPPER is completed by UPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Leonardo da Vinci's famous mural in Milan showing Christ's final meal.

clue.text: Part of film may be true, it's said

indicators.note: the clue tells us a word is spoken, so we want a word with the same sound

parts.note: genuine, real

explanation.surface: A claim that a section of a movie might be authentic.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a spool of film, and a feature was once shown as several such spools.

clue.text: Description of a nobleman taking in clubs

indicators.note: one piece takes in, or contains, another

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A story about an aristocrat who joins some clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts C inside A COUNT, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a report or narrative describing events, a synonym of description.

clue.text: Report of armistice in newspaper article

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so we want a word sounding like this one

parts.note: an armistice brings peace

explanation.surface: News of a ceasefire printed in a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists call an individual article a piece, as in a feature piece.

clue.text: I pay con woman for arranging ship's ladder

indicators.note: arranging letters puts them into a new order

explanation.surface: Paying a female fraudster to fix up a vessel's steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' reorders the twelve letters of I PAY CON WOMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A companionway is the staircase or ladder between decks on a ship.

clue.text: Flipping lair must contain rats? It doesn't matter

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it
flipping turns the word over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair
rats are vermin

explanation.surface: An exasperated shrug about a rat-infested hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reverses the lair to NED, and 'must contain' places the rats after its opening N, before the closing D.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a dismissive phrase meaning forget it, the matter is unimportant.

clue.text: Cycled round hot southern island

indicators.note: one piece goes round another, enclosing it

parts.note: rode, as on a bicycle
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cycling tour round a sunny Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts H inside RODE to give RHODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean, home of the ancient Colossus.

clue.text: French woman almost checked out after years

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first
almost all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: vetted, examined carefully

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman nearly cleared by security after years of waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final D from VETTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Yvette is a French female forename, so it is an example of a French woman.

clue.text: Back last nag, not the first

parts.note: the end is the last part

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A punter backing the horse that came in last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' takes H from HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a person or plan is to support or back it.

clue.text: Discarded stuff from planes in the morning

parts.note: jets are aeroplanes
AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: Rubbish dropped from aircraft early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard from a ship, hence any discarded material.

clue.text: Tablet unfortunately crushed in field

indicators.note: an unfortunate turn of events leaves these letters jumbled

parts.note: ground, as coffee beans are

explanation.surface: A pill sadly ground up out in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of battle is where fighting happens, so field here means the place of conflict.

clue.text: Unable to move quickly

definitions.meaning: stuck firm, as in held tight

explanation.surface: Stuck, yet speedy: a contradiction in four words.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means firmly fixed in place, as in stuck firm, and also rapidly.

clue.text: Come up a slope

parts.note: a rise is an upward slope

explanation.surface: An invitation to climb an incline.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise is to come up or appear, as a problem does.

clue.text: Nobleman briefly getting attention

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman

explanation.surface: A peer getting a quick hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the final L from EARL.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone's ear is to have their attention, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Second smoked herring for captain

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring, a British breakfast fish

explanation.surface: Another smoked fish served to the ship's master.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the captain of a boat or a sports team.

clue.text: Paddy, dry, swallowing an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: one piece swallows the other, holding it inside

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: An Irishman on the wagon who downs a drink anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irishman's name, but in British English a paddy is a fit of temper; TT stands for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean an outburst of bad temper; paddy is the British informal synonym.

clue.text: Group's leader cutting dreadful lament

indicators.note: the letter cuts into the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: dire means dreadful

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter of the word

explanation.surface: A band's frontman interrupting a terrible mournful song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts G inside DIRE, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song or lament for the dead.
